h2: Eddy current testing around Seattle: the assets, the rules and how a job is scoped
html:
Eddy current testing around Seattle: the assets, the rules and how a job is scoped

In the Seattle area, eddy current testing is used mostly on aluminum airframe structure, on non-ferrous heat exchanger tubing at the Puget Sound refineries, and on naval and commercial ship components. Atlantis is a Houston-based NDT company that sends crews to the site, with procedures reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III. Each job is quoted from the scope, the tube or part count and the governing document.

Airframes and the supplier base. Boeing builds the 737 in Renton, and the 767, 777 and 777X in Everett next to Paine Field. Boeing Field in south Seattle handles flight test and delivery. Around these sites are suppliers and repair stations where eddy current is the standard surface method on aluminum. Typical work is bolt-hole inspection with rotating probes, crack checks along fastener rows, and conductivity readings that confirm heat-treat condition after a repair or heat exposure. Aircraft work follows the OEM nondestructive test manual and the FAA maintenance rules in 14 CFR Parts 43 and 145. The airframer's supplier requirements decide whose personnel certification is accepted. Where a contract calls for NAS 410, Atlantis provides Level 3 support only through an associate, and says so before a job is accepted.

Refinery exchanger bundles. Five Washington refineries supply most of the region's fuel: BP at Cherry Point, Phillips 66 at Ferndale, Marathon and HF Sinclair at Anacortes, and U.S. Oil & Refining in Tacoma. Their copper-nickel, admiralty brass, stainless and titanium tubes are screened with bobbin-coil eddy current at turnarounds. Array or rotating probes then size the indications that decide whether tubes are plugged or bundles retubed. Carbon steel tubes do not respond well to conventional eddy current, so those bundles go to IRIS tube inspection or to remote-field testing. The exchanger shells are unfired pressure vessels under the Washington Department of Labor & Industries boiler and pressure vessel rules (chapter 70.79 RCW and chapter 296-104 WAC). Those rules let owner-user programs follow NBIC or API 510 inspection intervals.

Shipyards and naval work. Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility in Bremerton maintains carriers and submarines across six dry docks. Vigor's Harbor Island yard in Seattle repairs Navy and commercial ships in three dry docks. Naval NDT follows NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 instead of ASME, and the shipyard or prime contractor sets the personnel requirements. On commercial hulls, weld-probe eddy current and ACFM find surface cracks without stripping the paint system. That matters during a short docking slot.

Wet-climate insulation. Insulation in the Puget Sound lowlands stays damp for much of the year, which is the condition corrosion under insulation needs. Pulsed eddy current measures average wall thickness through insulation and jacketing. It is used to choose where insulation should come off, so the whole line does not have to be stripped.

  • Aluminum structure: bolt holes, fastener rows and conductivity after heat damage
  • Non-ferrous exchanger and condenser tubing at the Washington refineries
  • Carbon steel tubing: IRIS rather than conventional eddy current
  • Insulated piping and vessels: pulsed eddy current screening before insulation removal
  • Naval work: NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 requirements

Where to go next. Most searches that reach this page are about eddy current testing companies and services in general, not Seattle in particular. The national service is described on the eddy current testing page. Outage packages are on turnaround and shutdown inspection, and sector detail is on aerospace NDT in Seattle and marine NDT in Seattle. To learn the method, see eddy current training and the eddy current simulator. To scope a Puget Sound job, send the asset list and governing document through the eddy current enquiry form for Seattle.
